newsitem.title: UK: Britain to decide soon on Zaire force.
newsitem.headline: Britain to decide soon on Zaire force.

text.p: Britain will make a preliminary decision in the next "couple of days" whether or not to contribute to a proposed international force in eastern Zaire, officials said on Tuesday.

"The departments concerned are looking at a range of options to see if (Britain) should contribute to the multi-national force. I expect that over the next couple of days, ministers will take preliminary judgements," one British official said.
"It looks likely that there will be an international force and there will be interest here in contributing to it if we can, (and) if there is a workable military plan."

U.N. special envoy Raymond Chretien said earlier that approval for a Canadian-led multinational force to open up humanitarian corridors in eastern Zaire in order to bring relief to starving refugees could come within a week.
Canada has offered to lead the force but the United States and Britain have yet to make up their minds on joining.
"Militarily the U.S. decision is going to be very important," the official said.

"It is far from clear that there is a straightforward military and civilian situation into which a force could be inserted," the official added. "We are potential contributors but we have not made up our minds."
U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali said he expected more than 12 countries would make up the force and hoped that the United States would provide logistical support.

France has pushed for troops to be sent to Zaire to open humanitarian corridors to get food and water to starving Rwandan and Burundian refugees and displaced Zaireans, criticising the United States and other nations for dragging their feet.

The British official said the international force would have to have a clear mandate to prevent death and illness as well as to ensure that as many refugees returned home as possible. The force would also need a timetable for withdrawal.
